guarantees.claim: When any error_code bit is set (err_code[ErrInvalidOp], err_code[ErrInvalidIn], or err_code[ErrShadowUpdate] high), the corresponding hw2reg.err_code.*.de is asserted and hw2reg.err_code.*.d is driven to 1'b1.
When any fault_code bit is set (FaultKmacCmd, FaultKmacFsm, ...), the corresponding hw2reg.fault_status.*.de is asserted and hw2reg.fault_status.*.d is driven to 1'b1.
Signal fault_errs is the OR of all bits in reg2hw.fault_status; op_errs is the OR of all bits in err_code.

fault_err_req_d is set to 1 when fault_errs is high, cleared to 0 when fault_err_ack is high, and held at fault_err_req_q otherwise; op_err_req_d is set in the same pattern using op_errs and op_err_ack.

The prim_intr_hw instance u_intr_op_done generates interrupt output intr_op_done_o based on op_done event and CSR control signals reg2hw.intr_enable.q, reg2hw.intr_test.q, reg2hw.intr_test.qe, reg2hw.intr_state.q, and drives hw2reg.intr_state.de/d.

assumptions.claim: Inputs err_code and fault_code are stable, glitch-free, and only assert when a true error/fault condition exists.
assumptions.risk: Transient or spurious pulses could cause spurious status writes (d=1) and unexpected alert requests.

assumptions.claim: fault_err_ack and op_err_ack are driven by external logic (likely alert handler) and will eventually assert after a request is active, enabling the request signals to reset.
assumptions.risk: If ack never arrives, the request remains stuck high and downstream alert handling may stall or miss subsequent events.

assumptions.claim: op_done provides a valid pulse or level to indicate completion of an operation, conforming to prim_intr_hw requirements.
assumptions.risk: A missing or incorrect op_done signal could lead to missed interrupts, affecting software notification.

assumptions.claim: fault_err_req_q and op_err_req_q hold the registered state of the request signals and are updated elsewhere with the values of fault_err_req_d and op_err_req_d.
assumptions.risk: If these do not correctly store the previous state, the hold and clear logic for request generation breaks.

uncertain_points.claim: fault_err_req_q and op_err_req_q are used but not driven in this chunk; their registered behavior must be confirmed in another module to ensure the request hold/reset logic is correctly closed.
uncertain_points.cond: register update path outside this chunk
uncertain_points.risk: If the register is missing or incorrectly implemented, the request signals may not latch or clear as intended, possibly causing loss or hang of error/fault alerting.

uncertain_points.claim: The destination of fault_err_req_d and op_err_req_d is not shown; they are likely connected to different alert sender instances, but the comment hints at two types of alerts (hardware vs. software-generated). The handling and priority of these two request types need verification.
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect assignment could cause misrouted alerts, bypassing security escalation or masking a critical hardware fault as a software error.
